job.style: a description of a classroom activity or experiment and what it shows

passage: In our biology lab today, we explored how our bodies manage iron. We learned that anaemia is not a contagious disease like a cold, but a condition where the blood lacks enough healthy red blood cells to carry oxygen. While many believe only meat provides iron, our chart showed that green leafy vegetables like spinach and pulses are excellent plant-based sources. However, simply eating iron-rich food is not enough; our bodies need help to absorb it. We discovered that Vitamin C, found in citrus fruits like lemons, acts as a helper to increase iron absorption, whereas drinking tea immediately after a meal can block this process. We also discussed that iron-folic acid tablets are not just for the sick, but are a vital preventive measure for healthy students to maintain energy levels. Finally, we clarified that while milk is nutritious, it is not a primary source of iron, and relying on it alone will not prevent anaemia. Maintaining healthy iron levels requires a balanced diet, not just one 'superfood' or a single pill, and it is essential for both boys and girls to stay aware of their energy levels to prevent deficiency before it becomes severe.

items.evidence: We learned that anaemia is not a contagious disease like a cold, but a condition where the blood lacks enough healthy red blood cells to carry oxygen.
items.q: A doctor says Kavya has anaemia. What is actually wrong with her blood?
options: It lacks enough healthy red cells to carry oxygen
Her body simply has too little blood in it
It has no white blood cells left in it
It has picked up germs from a sick friend
items.explain: Anaemia means the blood lacks enough healthy red blood cells to carry oxygen; it is not caught like a cold.

wrong.why: thinks anaemia means having too little blood
confuses red blood cells with white blood cells
thinks anaemia spreads like a cold

items.evidence: We discovered that Vitamin C, found in citrus fruits like lemons, acts as a helper to increase iron absorption, whereas drinking tea immediately after a meal can block this process.
items.q: Anil eats spinach and dal for lunch. Which drink choice helps his body get the most iron from it?
options: Lemon juice taken along with the meal
A cup of tea right after the meal
A glass of milk, a complete food
No drink, as iron food is enough
items.explain: Vitamin C in lemons helps the body absorb iron, while tea right after a meal blocks it.

wrong.why: reverses the effect of tea on iron absorption
thinks milk is the best food against anaemia
misses that eating iron-rich food alone is not enough

items.evidence: We also discussed that iron-folic acid tablets are not just for the sick, but are a vital preventive measure for healthy students to maintain energy levels.
items.q: Priya is healthy, yet her school gives her iron-folic acid tablets. Why?
options: To prevent low iron and keep her energy up
Because extra iron always makes anyone healthier
Because periods are an illness that needs curing
Because only girls ever need any extra iron
items.explain: Iron-folic acid tablets are a preventive measure that help healthy students maintain their energy levels, not only a cure for the sick.

wrong.why: thinks more iron is always better
thinks menstruation is a disease causing anaemia
thinks boys never need extra iron

items.evidence: While many believe only meat provides iron, our chart showed that green leafy vegetables like spinach and pulses are excellent plant-based sources.
items.q: Ramesh is vegetarian and fears he cannot get enough iron. Which fact from the lesson helps him?
options: Spinach and pulses are good plant sources of iron
Milk gives all the iron a body needs
One plate of spinach cures anaemia at once
Lemons themselves contain the iron he needs
items.explain: The chart showed green leafy vegetables like spinach and pulses are excellent plant-based iron sources, so vegetarians can get iron.

wrong.why: thinks milk is the main iron source
thinks Vitamin C foods supply the iron itself
